newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch money rates unchanged, awaiting German M3.
newsitem.headline: Dutch money rates unchanged, awaiting German M3.

text.p: Dutch money rates were glued to previous levels on Monday and dealers said market players were waiting for the German M3 figure for January which could ignite a trimming of the German repo rate by five to ten basis points.
Dealers said a cut in the German repo would have only a slight effect on the Dutch market. They did not foresee a trimming of the Dutch special advances rate, which is comparable to the German repo.
"The German central bank might shave the repo rate, especially if the German M3 figure falls further.
The German M3 for January is expected to be announced from Wednesday February 19.
Analysts have not yet given any forecast for the January M3. But dealers were opting for a slight decrease from the 7.9 percent in December.

"This would spark a trimming of the repo," said one dealer, adding recent economic data from Germany, such as last week's high unemployment, had opened the way for a repo cut. The German repo has been pegged at 3.00 percent since last August.
Volumes in the Dutch market was somewhat low on Monday, with trades focusing on the short-end.
Call money rates were pinned at 2.88 percent bid. Three-month deposits were unchanged at 2.90 percent bid.
The guilder was steady against the mark at 112.3125 per 100 marks.
